NU/IR/SCO/2022-23/ 1470 April 04, 2026
Call for Expression of Interest (EOI) / Nominations
SCO Chair on Shared Buddhist Heritage
Nalanda University, an internationally acclaimed institution of higher learning under the
aegis of the Ministry of External Affairs, Government of India, invites Expressions of Interest
(EOI) / nominations from distinguished Indian scholars for the prestigious SCO Chair on
Shared Buddhist Heritage.
This Chair has been instituted as a significant academic initiative aligned with India’s
engagement with the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO), aiming to promote research,
dialogue, and academic collaboration on shared Buddhist heritage across SCO member
countries.
Eligibility Criteria:
• The applicant must be an eminent scholar of Indian nationality.
• Must hold the position of Professor or equivalent in a recognized institution of higher
education.
• Demonstrated expertise and significant contribution in the field of Buddhist Studies
or allied disciplines.
• Minimum 8-10 years of experience at the level of Professor.
• Age limit between 55 and 75 years.
Roles and Responsibilities:
The selected Chair will be expected to:
• Undertake high-quality research on themes related to shared Buddhist heritage.
• Develop and deliver lectures, seminars, and academic programmes.
• Foster international academic collaboration among SCO member states.
• Contribute to policy and scholarly discourse in the domain.
Emoluments and Tenure:
• Consolidated remuneration of ₹3,00,000/- per month.
• Additional benefits and entitlements as per University norms.
Application Process:
Interested candidates may submit their Expression of Interest along with:
• Detailed Curriculum Vitae
• Teaching Plan
• Research Plan
Applications should be sent within 21 days from the date of publication of this advertisement
to the email : recruitment@nalandauniv.edu.in. The selection will be made in accordance with
the prescribed norms and regulations governing the SCO Chair.
Nalanda University reserves the right to accept or reject any application without assigning
any reason.
